headline: International segment drives earnings outperformance
summary: Lenskart posted strong revenue growth of 34% yoy, driven by 31% yoy growth in the India business and 38% yoy growth in the international business. India gross margin was up 74 bps yoy and EBITDA margin expanded 197 bps yoy. International gross margin/EBITDA margin increased 111/506 bps yoy. The company exceeded our pre-Ind AS EBITDA estimate by 9.2% and EPS estimate by 14%. We upgrade our FY2027-29 EPS estimates by 9-15%, as we bake in higher revenue growth and margin expansion for both segments. This drives a revised DCF-based FV of Rs615 (Rs560 earlier). Retain ADD.
source: Source: Bloomberg, Company data, Kotak Institutional Equities estimates
priceNote: Prices in this report are based on the market close of August 12, 2026

content.text: Strong 34% yoy revenue growth, driven by India and international segments
Lenskart’s revenue grew 34% yoy, with both the India and international
businesses reporting strong growth. Segmentally, (1) India business revenue
increased 31% yoy, led by a 23% yoy rise in eyewear units sold and remainder
by an ASP increase, also demonstrated by healthy SSSG of 18% and (2)
international business revenue rose 38% yoy, led by a 34% yoy rise in eyewear
units sold. According to Lenskart, it will continue to focus on network expansion
and improved merchandising to structurally drive future growth.
Higher GM and operating leverage drive 374 bps yoy EBITDA margin expansion
Lenskart reported overall gross margin of 70.3% in 1QFY27 (versus 68.7% in
1QFY26). The company managed to offset the currency headwind by increasing
reliance on in-house manufacturing. Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin was at 13.3%,
registering a strong expansion of 374 bps yoy. Segmentally, (1) India business
EBITDA margin expanded 197 bps yoy and pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin expanded
208 bps yoy and (2) international EBITDA margin increased 506 bps yoy and
pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin expanded 620 bps yoy. EBITDA margin expansion
was driven by gross margin expansion and operating leverage from marketing
and other fixed expenses.
Healthy store expansion, large opportunity ahead
Other highlights include (1) India store count increasing to 2,725 from 2,609
stores in 4QFY26 and 2,137 stores in 1QFY26. Of its 2,725 stores, 1,067 stores
were in metro cities and (2) international store count rising to 734 from 718
stores in 4QFY26 and 669 stores in 1QFY26. Stores were added across Japan,
Southeast Asia and the Middle East. Lenskart is witnessing strong revenue
ramp-up and SSSG in metro and non-metro stores in India. The company
believes there is clear potential to add 10k+ stores in India across existing and
new cities.
Retain ADD with a revised FV of Rs615
Lenskart is on a strong revenue growth trajectory, which is driving operating
leverage. We account for stronger-than-expected 1Q performance, particularly
in the international segment. We upgrade our FY2027-29 revenue estimates by
~3% and EPS estimates by 9-15%. This, coupled with a roll forward to
September 2027, drives a revised DCF-based FV of Rs615. Retain ADD.

Key takeaways from earnings call  Management guidance. Management maintained its guidance for long-term, steady-state pre-Ind AS
EBITDA margin of ~25%.
 Gross margin. A meaningful share of Lenskart’s frame procurement is sourced from China—so the

depreciation of INR against RMB exerts direct pressure on the cost of goods. Despite this, the product margin has continued to be resilient in both the India and international businesses through (1) growing premiumization and, increasingly, (2) a higher proportion of in-house manufacturing. At a consolidated level, the product margin crossed 70% for the first time this quarter, helped in part by a seasonally heavier international sunglasses mix.
 Alongside its own manufacturing, vendor relationships and the volume-based cost efficiencies that
come with scale are equally important levers to absorb input cost pressures. Management will
focus on negotiations with vendors to improve product margins.
 Manufacturing. Lenskart’s long-term goal is self-reliance in frame and lens manufacturing. This
quarter, the company increased its investment in Baofeng Framekart, its China frame-manufacturing JV, to add in-house capacity. The Hyderabad facility will be the next major step-up in this journey.

According to management, as more of the manufacturing is in-house, the impact of currency movements on the cost base will keep reducing.
Lenskart has been shifting more manufacturing to its Indian facilities
Snapshot of Lenskart’s in-house manufacturing
 Eye tests. Lenskart conducts free eye tests to increase the size of the market. Management believes

eye testing is the biggest driver of the 23% volume growth in India. A significant majority of customers who do an eye test at Lenskart will purchase eyeglasses from the store, either immediately or within a few months. Management noted that customers who get an eye test for the first time take longer to make their purchase. It is possible that as the volume of eye tests increases, the conversion rates will drop and the company will have to work on improving rates.
 India business. In 1QFY27, the India business reported revenue growth of 31% yoy. The revenue

growth was primarily volume-driven, with eyewear units growing 23% yoy. This was powered by a 43% yoy increase in the eye tests conducted. ASP contributed a 6.4% increase yoy, driven by customers choosing premium lens options and not just by price increases. The SSSG came in at 18% in 1Q, driven by volume expansion from new customers acquired and also deepening relationships with gold members, driving repeat purchases. Gold membership now has 9 mn+ active members.
 Market size. According to management, as India urbanizes, studies longer and lives on screens,
the market size keeps growing. ~780 mn Indians need vision correction today, heading toward
~940 mn by FY2030E. Daily, 35k Indians get tested at Lenskart for the first time and discover they
need prescription eyewear.
 Growth. According to management, supply and not demand, is the constraint in India. Management
noted that while there is a large opportunity for store expansion in Tier 2+ regions, it requires better
understanding of the logistics, finding manpower for these stores, hiring optometrists and more.
Remote optometry has enabled Lenskart to expand faster; management is also investing in AI eye
testing to solve constraints related to Tier 2+ store expansion.
 Network expansion (1/2). Lenskart has grown in three directions, i.e., (1) deeper in the pin codes
it already served, (2) wider into unserved pin codes within existing cities and (3) into new towns. In
the 1,517 pin codes that already had a Lenskart store in 2QFY26, density rose from 1.5 to 1.6 stores
per pin code in nine months and the same stores kept growing, with SSSG of ~18% and SPSG of
~24%. Of the 2,821 unserved pin codes in 2QFY26 mapped in Lenskart’s existing cities, it entered
152 and opened 155 stores. 2,669 unserved pin codes remain, as of 1QFY27. It opened up stores
in 140 Tier 2+ towns that Lenskart had never entered, with 142 stores in towns such as Hassan in
Karnataka, Balasore in Odisha, Tura in Meghalaya and Gandhidham in Gujarat. According to GeoIQ,
there are an additional 3,644 viable new Tier 2+ towns for Lenskart to enter.
 Network expansion (2/2). Management noted that despite the net addition of 455 stores in the
past nine months, it only covered ~5% of the 6,400 pin codes it had identified in 2QFY26.
Management noted that most of its stores are still relatively young and can continue to grow at a
healthy rate, given the high demand in India.

 Premiumization. According to management, prescription eyeglasses with premium lenses form a
healthy share of the overall business. Owndays lenses have captured a significant share of the
premium price point. Owndays premium lenses now generate over Rs15 bn annually in prescription
eyeglass sales. Lenskart also has a luxury lens portfolio: Rodenstock and Tokai. Rodenstock is a
century-old German optical house and Tokai is Japan's neuroscience-led lens maker. Volumes of
this portfolio grew over 35% yoy combined in 1QFY27; together they generated Rs2.5 bn in
prescription eyeglass sales last year. The frame portfolio is premiumizing too, with Meller on track
to be a ~US$70 mn brand globally for sunglasses alone.
 Progressive Lens. The progressive lens market has a distinct and growing share of volume,
addressing presbyopia—where eyeglasses coverage in India is as low as ~25%. Lenskart has
digitized progressive eye testing and units grew 33% yoy in 1QFY27.
 Value-eyewear. The company has launched glasses priced at Rs500, sold profitably through Hustlr
Club. According to management, lower-priced products are more margin accretive and will not
dilute profitability as the business scales.
 ASP. India ASP grew 6.4% yoy in 1Q to Rs1,856, driven by a continued shift in product mix toward
premium products and progressive lenses.
 International business. Its revenue grew 38% yoy. While the business benefited from favorable

currency tailwinds, the underlying momentum remains strong. On a constant-currency basis, 1Q clocked revenue growth of ~29% yoy. This growth was broad-based, with robust performance across Japan, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and its other geographies. In the international business, the store addition will gradually accelerate once the unit economics improves.
 Growth. Volume was the primary driver of growth; eyewear units grew 37.6% yoy. Additionally,
sunglasses had a pronounced seasonal quarter, with units growing 58% yoy and nearly doubling
sequentially, as April-June is the segment's seasonal peak, amplified by Meller's fast-growing
online channel.
 ASP. The ASP was roughly flat yoy at Rs5,267. On a constant-currency basis, ASP would have
declined, reflecting this quarter's heavier sunglasses mix, a structurally lower-ASP category.
 Profitability. According to management, international has structurally higher product margins than
the India business, which should translate into even higher profitability as it scales. The
international business has a higher product margin than the India business, as international ASP
is 3X of India, while the ACP is 2X. In 1QFY27, the pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin expansion of 620 bps
was driven by (1) operating leverage and (2) product margin expansion. The margin was also driven
by higher sales of sunglasses this quarter, which carry a structurally higher margin.

 Smart glasses. Lenskart opened early access for its smart glasses in 4QFY26; sign-ups crossed 80k.

The B Smart glasses are priced at Rs22k and have photo and video capture, open-ear audio, Google Gemini integration with multilingual support and prescription-lens capability. The product will be available for sale across Lenskart stores very soon, so customers can experience it before purchasing.
 Currency risk. In the India business, a significant proportion of frames are imported and that has a

currency risk. Lenskart’s international business provides a natural hedge to some extent and it is a net importer from that perspective. For the long term, the company is accelerating its in-house manufacturing for frames. This will reduce its exposure to currency on the negative side.
Key changes to estimates
We upgrade our FY2027-29 revenue estimates by ~3% and EPS estimates by 9-15%.
We raise EPS by 9-15% for FY2027-29E
